design:
Decision records. Each gives the decision, the alternative rejected and why. HOW beyond this belongs to the build.

D1. A task's work is its own branch and the evidence it recorded.
- Rejected: keep joining by requirement and filter out siblings case by case (F520 already tried this with "only once that task is approved").
- Why: a requirement is shared by design (a drive task covers every requirement it drives); a commit is not. A case-by-case filter answers "whose commit?" from the wrong key and failed again on 10-29.
- Requirement links keep saying what a task *serves* (coverage and the completion gate). F520's clause is retired (operator, 2026-10-29).

D2. Fix the one answer, `merge_targets`, rather than each reader.
- Rejected: patch only the completion check's fallback (project_checks.py:1794) to prefer the branch tip.
- Why: five readers route through `merge_targets` (completion check, review target, approval check, prerequisite top-up, approval refusal). Patching one leaves gap 2, and lets the readers disagree about what approval merges, which is the drift D12 of task-dependencies exists to prevent.

D3. A run counts as alive when it is in the Hub's run registry, the test the stuck_task scan already uses (stalls.py:814), and the reset refusal uses the same test.
- Rejected: a heartbeat or worktree-activity timeout.
- Why: the heartbeat is written by nothing (stalls.py:814 comment), and worktree quiet is exactly the guess that made the mender reset a live run.

D4. A task added to a running build takes the build's default builder and checker, shown as "by default" (operator, 2026-10-29).
- Rejected: requiring the adding agent to name both, or holding the task for the operator.
- Why: one adds friction to every reviewer's add, the other stalls the flow on the operator. The "by default" mark keeps a wrong default visible.

D5. A send-back carries a reason class and a sentence, required from reviewers and set by the Hub on its own send-backs.
- Rejected: deriving the class from the failing pieces.
- Why: the cases that lost their reason on 10-29 named no failing piece, so there was nothing to derive from. Per-piece rejection text stays as built.

D6. No separate acceptance-drive task.
- Rejected: the usual first drive task every other task waits on.
- Why: it serves every requirement. Until task 1 is live in the running Hub, its evidence would stand in for each build task's work, which is the defect being fixed. Each task carries its own failing-first tests instead; approval will warn `no_acceptance_drive`. The live replay (ac-live-replay) runs after a Hub restart onto the change.

Hazards and rollback:
- **What reaches master (Tier 2).** FR-1/FR-3 change what approval merges. Risk: a build that relied on a sibling's evidence merging through another task's approval stops merging that work. That is visible as an approval that merges nothing ("already in" or "nothing to merge"), not as wrong code landing. Rollback: revert the task 1 commit. No data is rewritten; existing evidence and integration rows are untouched.
- **Likely migration (FR-8).** Storing a reason class on a transition probably needs a nullable column on task_transitions. Old rows stay NULL and show "no reason recorded". Rollback: the migration's downgrade drops the column. The migration must follow `.claude/rules/` (migration checklist).
- **Hub restart.** All of this is Hub code. Agents build on their branches; nothing takes effect in the running :8000 Hub until the operator merges to master and restarts it, and that restart runs the migration on live data. Back up the database before that restart (VACUUM INTO, per .claude/reference/hubs.md).
- **Reviewer contract (FR-9).** A send-back without a class is refused, so an agent prompt that does not know the classes will see a refusal. The refusal names the six classes, so the agent can retry in the same turn.

problem:
Found by reading the ledger of the flow "The build plan lives in the spec, and every task goes to its people" (spdoc-a7d41f10be14) on 2026-10-29. Its six tasks had four send-backs, and two of them were produced or made worse by the Hub itself.

1. **The completion check checked the wrong commit.** task-40ed6157e1c5 ("Refuse a second driver") completed with its own work at 3d25ad3. The check (chk-d9d91d70e0c7) targeted 65ae915, the acceptance-drive task's commit. Its tree matched an earlier run, so it reused that pass without running anything. The change broke two existing Hub tests; QA found them 80 minutes later. The second and third completions (19:14, 19:37) ran no check at all: the stand-in commit had landed on master by then, so `unmerged()` left nothing to check. Cause, read in code: `project_checks.check_targets` asks `task_integration.merge_targets`, which joins evidence by requirement (`_targets`, task_integration.py:307-352). The drive task's accepted FR-7 evidence therefore became the F1083 task's "work". The fallback to the task's own branch tip (project_checks.py:1794-1802) fires only when that answer is empty.
2. **A task was sent back for a merge it never needed.** task-dac742f3f922 depends on the drive task and "Plan in the spec", both already landed. Approval was refused with 409 because its branch lacked 00fe846. That is task-40ed6157e1c5's commit, labelled "prerequisite task-94d59bc7214d's commit". Cause: `task_workspace._prerequisite_commits` asks `merge_targets` for the prerequisite's work, and once task-40ed6157e1c5 was approved its FR-7 evidence counted as the drive task's work (the F520 clause "or by tasks already approved"). The send-back cost one build turn and one review turn, with nothing wrong in the code.
3. **The mender reset a task whose run was alive.** At 17:39 the stall check reported loop-7e7ab7938538 as no_progress ("no run started and no task changed status since 17:07"). DeveloperOpus's run on task-799357e3e80e was executing from 17:02 to 18:02. The mender guessed "the run died" from a quiet worktree and moved the task in_progress -> assigned. `mend_reset_task` accepted it.
4. **A task added mid-build has nobody.** QA added task-4161311000e6 ("Board card names each build task's checker") during review. It has no assignee, no builder and no checker, in the very build whose subject is that every task goes to its people.
5. **A send-back that names no failing piece loses its reason.** task-40ed6157e1c5's second send-back (a real regression) and task-dac742f3f922's (a merge only) both read "Evidence: ... held (not named as failing)" in the task history. Why the task came back survives only in the reviewer's notes and turn output, so telling a defect from a merge or a flake took database queries.

Already fixed, and not part of this change: per-piece evidence verdicts. Up to 2026-10-27 a send-back rejected every piece from the commit with one copied reason (for example run-ebcd966c87db: 13 rejections, 1 distinct reason). Since 2026-10-28 ("Verdicts judge each piece", task-980250864260) only the named pieces are rejected, each with its own reason, and the rest are held (for example run-c830ab15f653: 3 rejections, 3 reasons). The vault fact fct-bfdeee9417b9 still states the old rule and has been reported (rpt-f3cd6f900172).

Who it hurts: the operator, who pays for turns that fix nothing and gets regressions past a gate that claims to check them; and every reviewer, whose verdict becomes the only real check.

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-29 the F1083 task's completion check ran on the drive task's commit and reused a pass, so a change breaking two existing tests passed the gate. Retires F520's 'or by tasks already approved' (operator, 2026-10-29).
requirements.statement: The commits that a task's completion check, review turn and approval check treat as the task's work are the task's own: the newest commit on its branch and commits named by evidence it recorded. A commit named by evidence another task recorded, including against a requirement both tasks serve and including after that task is approved, never counts as this task's work.

requirements.rationale: The F1083 task's second and third completions recorded no check run at all.
requirements.statement: Every move of a task to completed, including each one after a send-back, either records a check run whose target contains that completion's newest branch commit, or says in the task's history why no check ran. It never skips silently because a stand-in commit is already on the main branch.

requirements.rationale: task-dac742f3f922 was sent back for lacking 00fe846, a commit of a task it does not depend on.
requirements.statement: The work a dependent task's checkout takes in from a prerequisite, and the work approval requires the dependent's branch to contain, are commits produced by that prerequisite task. A commit produced by a task the dependent does not depend on, directly or through its prerequisites, is never required.
A 'Bring in prerequisite work' commit made by the Hub names the task that produced the commit it merges.
The stall scan does not report a loop or flow as having made no progress while a run on one of its tasks is executing.

requirements.rationale: The mender reset task-799357e3e80e at 17:39 while DeveloperOpus's run was executing (17:02-18:02).
requirements.statement: Resetting a task (mend_reset_task, or any route that moves an in_progress task back to assigned or pending) while a run on that task is executing is refused. The refusal names the run, its agent and when it started, and the task is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: task-4161311000e6 was added during review with no assignee, builder or checker.
requirements.statement: A task added to a running build, by any agent or by an amendment, takes the build's default builder and checker unless the addition names them. The board shows each as 'by default' when it came that way.

requirements.rationale: Two send-backs on 2026-10-29, one a regression and one a merge only, both read just 'held (not named as failing)' in the history.
requirements.statement: Every move of a task to revision_needed records a reason class (defect, regression, broken-check, merge-needed, evidence-only or flaky) and a sentence of reason, whether or not it names failing pieces. The class and sentence appear in the task's history in the app and in task_history.

A reviewer's send-back without a reason class is refused, naming the classes. A send-back the Hub makes itself (checks or a landing batch) records broken-check, or flaky when a confirming re-run passed.

summary: The Hub decides which commits are "a task's work" through the evidence recorded against the task's requirements. When two tasks in one build share a requirement, which happens whenever an acceptance-drive task covers the requirements it drives, one task's commit stands in for the other's. That stand-in is what gets checked at completion, required as a prerequisite merge, and counted at approval. This change makes a task's work its own commits and makes every completion check that work. It also makes the mender unable to reset a task whose run is alive, gives a task added mid-build the build's people, and makes every send-back say why in the task's history.
